answer: Each agent must prove 4 GiB of memory-hard work that stays resident for ninety seconds per epoch, keyed to a fresh salt. Paging the working set out costs a 40 percent slowdown, so every extra fake pins another 4 GiB of live RAM at the same moment. Even a farm sited in a karst cavern or a juniper-lined canyon hits a hard ceiling, because each identity needs its own pinned memory at once.
